question: Who according to the tribals of Chota Nagpur were referred to as the 'Dikus'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Outsiders.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tribals of Chota Nagpur were referred to as the '**Dikus**' means **Outsiders**.
 
• They see the Dikus in the form of Moneylenders, Zamindars, revenue officials, etc.
 
• When the use of Money circulated the role of a new group like money lenders came in.
 
• Tribes viewed these outsiders as oppressors and were against them.
 
• Tribes attacked police stations and churches and raided the property of moneylenders and Zamindars.
 
• These revolts over the period forced the colonial government to introduce laws so that the land of the tribals could not be easily taken over by Dikus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are many tribal groups are there in Chota Nagpur.
 
• Half the tribals belong to six large tribes are **Gond, Bhil, Santal, Oraon, Mina, and Munda.**
 
• About a tenth of India's tribals, **3.4 million, reside in Chota Nagpur, and another 1,154,000 in nearby Santal Parganas.**
